title: Waystones and Travel
summary: Where waystones and Wayshrines are, how to attune and travel, what it costs, and the other ways to get around.

s.x: A
waystone

is a stone you can attune to and later travel back to. Once you have attuned to a few, you can jump between them, or home to Skyhaven, for a small number of XP levels. They are the backbone of long trips in the survival world, so it pays to attune to every one you walk past.
Waystones stand in three kinds of place:
Wayshrines:

small ruined shrines of mossy stone brick with a waystone on a dais, candles, broken pillars and a chest. They generate in forests, taiga, savanna, plains, sunflower plains, meadows, snowy plains, deserts, birch forests and cherry groves.
Villages:
the first time a village's bell area loads, a waystone is placed two to four blocks from the bell.
Dungeons:
every dungeon entrance has one, including the Infernal Citadel in the Nether and the Astral Observatory in the End.
Skyhaven has one as well, just left of the spawn point.
Waystones are unbreakable outside creative mode, so you cannot lose one by accident.
Wayshrines are common: the world is cut into 24-chunk (384-block) squares and each can hold one, at least 8 chunks from the next. The
Shrine Chest
in each holds 2 to 4 stacks from bread, apples, cooked beef, carrots, torches, arrows, string, sticks and iron nuggets, plus 1 to 2
Runic Dust
and a map. Like dungeon chests, it is rolled per player, so everyone who visits gets their own loot.
Walk up to a waystone and
right-click
it.
The first time, it lights up (a lit waystone glows brighter), you get a
WAYSTONE ATTUNED
banner with its name, and it is added to your list and to your map.
Right-click it again to open the travel menu.
Waystones get an automatic name: the dungeon it guards,
<Name> Village
, or a made-up place name followed by the biome, for example "Ravenwatch · Taiga".
You can
rename
a waystone by right-clicking it while holding a name tag with a name of up to 32 characters. The name tag is used up, and the new name is shown to everyone.
The menu lists
Skyhaven
first (outside the hub) and then every waystone you have attuned to, with its world, distance and coordinates. Click one to go.

rows.x: From Skyhaven to any attuned waystone
1 XP level per 1,000 blocks of distance, plus 1 (maximum 5)

s.x: That means anything under 1,000 blocks costs 1 level, 1,000 to 1,999 costs 2, and so on up to the 5-level cap at 4,000 blocks. Creative players travel for free.
You land on a free spot next to the destination waystone, facing it. A few rules:
You must still be within 6 blocks of the waystone when you click, and you need enough XP levels.
If a waystone no longer exists, you get "That waystone is gone" and it drops off your list.
Destinations are saved on you, so your list follows you between worlds and dimensions.
Choosing a destination does not take you there at once:
In combat
the trip is refused (see
Combat basics
Otherwise you
stand still for 5 seconds
with a countdown in the action bar, a ring of sparkles and a tick each second. Moving more than about a third of a block, taking damage or getting into a fight cancels it, and you keep your XP.
The XP levels are paid when you arrive, not when you click.
Creative players skip the wait. Going back to Skyhaven has the same one 5 second wait, not two.
Attune to a waystone before you head into a
danger region
or dungeon. When your health is low, the trip home costs at most 5 levels, which is far cheaper than a death run back through monsters.
Waystone icons on the world map can be clicked for
Track
and
Share in chat
, which makes it easy to tell a friend where to meet you. See
Waypoints
